input.question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?
input.ground_truth: America didn't get bombed and saw *immense* federal spending that ended the great depression. Also, as it turns out, being the only industrial power that didn't get bombed to hell makes your economy pretty strong as there isn't a whole lot of competition.

Question: After World War 2 how did America end up with their economy improved and the rest of the world ended up broke?

Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a big game together. During the game (which is like World War 2), you (America) have a really big house with lots of toys, food, and tools. Your friends (other countries) use up many of their toys and food to help play the game and fight with you and against you.

When the game ends, your house (America) is still in good shape because you didn’t use up all your stuff. You even helped your friends a little bit while the game was happening, and after the game, you give them some of your extra toys and food to help them fix their houses.

Meanwhile, your friends’ houses are all messy and broken because they used up almost everything they had during the game. They don’t have many toys or food left.

So, after the game, your house (America) is nice and full again, but your friends’ houses (other countries) need a lot of help to get better.

That’s how America’s economy got better after World War 2, while many other countries were poor and needed help to rebuild.
